sanitizedEvidence.summary: After a clean OpenBlade-only Service restart reset the validation manifest's per-process one-shot guard, a fresh baseline bound exact RZ09-0581 identity, BIOS 4.00 provenance, Balanced and Automatic, admitted full power, physical pad absence, and zero blocked or unconfirmed writes.

An initial second-scenario arm in the already-used Service process was rejected by the validation manifest's per-process one-shot guard before the validation device command. No marker was created, HyperBoost was not confirmed, no cleanup was attempted, and a fresh baseline remained green. The Service was then restarted cleanly before the successful arm.
The restarted installed Service applied HyperBoost once, confirmed mode 7, finalized durable padless ownership, and created the private marker without cleanup or manual recovery.

A bounded elevated helper verified the marker-bound OpenBlade Service identity and journal, forcibly terminated only that Service instance once, and confirmed SCM started one replacement instance from the same exact validation build.

Read-only FirmwareSmoke verification confirmed stable Balanced and Automatic state, a retired journal, the exact installed generation, and exactly one matching Service recovery attempt and completion.

Private marker, diagnostics, deployment, boundary, and verification files remain uncommitted. The exact production Service assembly was restored and a final read-only baseline confirmed Balanced, Automatic, zero blocked or unconfirmed writes, and a retired journal.

limitations: This run validates one installed-Service unexpected-exit recovery on exact RZ09-0581 hardware with BIOS 4.00 provenance, Balanced and Automatic, an admitted full-power adapter, and confirmed physical pad absence.
The intentional crash boundary covered only the marker-bound OpenBlade Service. No Razer service or unrelated process was changed.
The companion exact-generation low-power annotation is required for cumulative production admission.
